The single wave application is named in coverage_exclusions with its reason, so G-RR's coverage check can excuse it explicitly instead of reading an empty matrix as a silent gap. WHERE THE REAL FINDINGS LIVE: this dispatch was scope=intra-app, and the module-grain analysis it actually performed - all 15 unordered module pairs scored on entity / operation / persona / technology (weights 0.35 / 0.35 / 0.20 / 0.10, cluster threshold 60), one 3-member cluster found (insert-form, edit-form, view-form; weakest pairwise 74, cohesion 79, recommendation shared_service), three modules rejected from that cluster with their failing scores (46, 18, 10), and three source-of-truth conflicts - is written to the scope-matching artifact at rationalization/wave-3f6bdbb9-81fa-4fb9-845f-fb6a81ba2cbe/c70846ac-0948-4953-990c-c68a2be292d9/intra-app-redundancy.json. It is NOT restated at application grain here: doing so would produce a document that validates against this schema while meaning something entirely different from what its cross-app consumers read. METHOD AND LIMITS: no repository or tool was run by this pass; all upstream evidence came from the three staged Discovery artifacts (business-logic.json, structural-analysis.json, quality-risk.json), so no measurement here claims tool-run or repository-scan provenance - and with no pairs to score there is no measured percentage in this document at all. REGULATORY VARIANCE: not computable and not fabricated - zero of the application's 60 business rules trace to any regulation, and the faa profile's regulatory sources (14 CFR Parts 47, 61, 63, 67, 183) were determined not applicable upstream; that null result is recorded in the sibling regulatory-variance.json. PROFILE NOTE: the governing profile is faa per the authoritative dispatch declaration and the staged business-logic.json names the same profile, so there is no profile discrepancy introduced by this run; the separate observation that an aviation-regulator profile does not plausibly govern an academic student-records desktop tool was raised as a finding upstream in Discovery and is restated here only as context, not as a new claim.

The alternative - counting the application's 6 internal modules as 6 applications to clear a pairwise threshold - would redefine the unit of comparison, and every downstream consumer that resolves application ids against the wave roster would fail to bind them while the one real application read as uncovered.

review_asks.title: Three of the six parts of the Student Management System do the same job on the same student record - and they disagree with each other about the rules.
review_asks.why: This duplication is invisible in any portfolio-wide comparison, it changes the refactor estimate for this application, and three of the disagreements are producing wrong output or data loss today rather than merely costing maintenance effort.

confidence.rationale: Every claim rests on named file-and-line evidence from two independent upstream passes that corroborate each other: identical control counts in the two editor layouts, the ten-field mapping written twice, and three value-domain declarations that do not agree.

review_asks.assessment: The add, edit and list screens are three implementations of one job - creating, finding, changing and deleting the student record - over one ten-column table. The add and edit screens are effectively the same screen built twice: identical 24-control layouts and the same ten-field mapping written out twice, so any change to a field rule has to be made in two places. Separately, the list screen contains three different routines that all fill the same grid, and only one of them is exposed to the injection flaw. Three disagreements between the duplicated copies are worth investigating as business questions, not just code cleanup. (1) The add and edit screens offer three gender values but the dashboard counts only two, so any student recorded as 'Other' appears in no statistic and the tiles do not add up to the student population - and no total is shown anywhere that would reveal the gap. (2) The admission-year list on the entry screens stops at 2023 and the dashboard's year tiles are computed from a hardcoded 2023, so every year tile has been wrong since January 2024 and the error grows by one year annually with no warning. (3) The roll number can be freely typed when adding a student but cannot be changed when editing one, so correcting a mistyped roll number requires deleting and re-creating the record, with no audit trail and no safety net.
review_asks.reasoning: Recorded here because this artifact is the cross-application matrix and it has nothing to say about this application - there was no peer to compare it against - so the one substantive redundancy finding for the wave would otherwise be invisible to a reviewer reading only this file. The finding itself was produced at module grain: all 6 internal modules compared pairwise on business entities handled, operations performed and human role served. Three modules clustered (add, edit, list screens; weakest pairwise score 74 against a 60 threshold), and three were ruled out with their scores recorded - the dashboard as a separate reporting concern (46-51), the database-connection module as duplicating nothing at all (18; 13 lines, zero queries), and the generated plumbing as having no data or user surface (10). The full evidence, all 15 pair scores and the contested anchor choice are in the intra-app artifact; this entry is a pointer, not a second assessment, and the anchor decision is put to the reviewer there rather than restated here.

evidence_refs.name: Duplicated editor
evidence_refs.detail: The two entry screens declare byte-for-byte identical 24-control layouts (373 vs 371 lines) and the ten-field parameter mapping is written twice (InsertForm.vb:12, EditForm.vb:54)

evidence_refs.name: Gender values disagree
evidence_refs.detail: Three values offered on the entry screens (Male/Female/Other) against two counted on the dashboard (Male/Female); no grand total is displayed anywhere that would expose the shortfall

evidence_refs.name: Year tiles frozen at 2023
evidence_refs.detail: All five academic-year tiles derive from a hardcoded currentYear = 2023 (Form1.vb:59) while the entry screens offer the fixed list 2019-2023 - wrong since 1 January 2024

evidence_refs.name: Triplicated list logic
evidence_refs.detail: The list screen fills the same grid from three routines (LoadData, LoadSData, RefreshData); only LoadSData builds its query from raw user text, and it is the application's only confirmed injection vector (ViewForm.vb:50)

review_asks.title: Cross-application redundancy scan recorded for the Student Management System: one application in the wave, no peer to compare against, so no cross-application overlap was computable.
review_asks.why: So the record shows that an empty cross-application matrix here means 'no peer existed to compare against', not 'this application was checked against the portfolio and found unique' - the two read identically in an empty file and lead to opposite decisions.

confidence.rationale: The input count is a direct observation, not an estimate: exactly one application's Discovery artifacts were staged, and all three required inputs for it were present and complete. The only reservation concerns what was NOT examined, which is stated explicitly rather than inferred.

review_asks.assessment: WHAT WAS SCANNED: one application, the Student Management System (VB.NET). WHAT WAS FOUND: no cross-application overlap, because there was no second application to compare it against - this dispatch staged exactly one application, so the number of application pairs available to score was zero and the overlap tables in this record are empty for that reason alone. This is reported as a finding and the application is named in the exclusions list with its reason, so it is not silently missing from the wave's coverage. WHAT THIS DOES NOT MEAN: it does not mean this application was tested against the portfolio and found to duplicate nothing. That question is still open and should be answered when a wave containing peer applications is analysed. WHAT WAS EXAMINED INSTEAD: the application was analysed on its own, part by part. All 6 of its internal parts were compared against each other - 15 comparisons, none skipped - and one duplicate group was found: the add, edit and list screens all manage the same student record and should become one component behind one shared service. Three parts were ruled out, each with its score recorded. Three disagreements between duplicated copies of the same rule were recorded as source-of-truth conflicts: the gender values, the admission-year definition, and whether the roll number can be changed. That detail lives in the companion internal-duplication record, not in this file, because mixing internal parts into an application-level table would make them look like separate applications to everything that reads this file downstream. ALSO ABSENT, STATED SO IT IS NOT MISTAKEN FOR A CLEAN RESULT: no regulatory consistency findings, because none of this application's 60 business rules trace to any regulation. The governing profile for this run is the FAA profile as declared; the upstream analysis recorded - as its own finding, restated here only as context - that an aviation-regulator profile does not obviously fit an academic student-records desktop tool. That is a profile-assignment question for a reviewer, not a conclusion of this scan.
review_asks.reasoning: The minimum-input guard was applied before any scoring: the wave bundle was counted and held one application with accessible Discovery artifacts, which at cross-application grain yields zero pairs. The artifact was still emitted, shaped honestly - true count of 1, empty overlap arrays, and the application named in coverage_exclusions with a reason, which is what converts an empty matrix into a stated finding that the coverage check can excuse. The count was NOT inflated by treating the application's 6 internal modules as 6 applications: that would redefine the unit the field measures, and every consumer resolving application ids against the wave roster would fail to bind the internal names while the one real application still read as uncovered. The honest number was emitted and the constraint it fails was reported instead. Evidence came entirely from the three staged Discovery analyses (60 business rules, the structural map, and the quality/risk assessment at debt 74/100, HIGH risk tier), which corroborate each other on the same file-and-line citations. No source repository or tool was run by this pass. Known gaps carried forward from upstream and not papered over: record counts and database column types were never resolved, and no unique index on the roll number could be confirmed.
